readingPaths.title: Turn choices into a canonical comparison
readingPaths.description: Begin with the same six elements throughout. A relation keeps every permitted output; removing the two ambiguities makes a well-defined isomorphism. The comparison then extends to a grid of decompositions. Other finite routes recover operators or count flags.

readingPaths.title: Repair a coordinate and test its limit
readingPaths.description: Try to turn nonlinear addition into ordinary addition. The first correction works; the next is blocked in characteristic three. Begin with the coefficient calculation, then use the coefficient-and-filtration study to organise its obstruction in a filtered complex.

readingPaths.title: Make a composition law visible
readingPaths.description: Compare two ways of exposing the same polynomial constraint. A free-module expansion gives a direct remainder calculation; generic fibres and Frobenius give a second route with different prerequisites.

readingPaths.title: Turn a numerical question into exact arithmetic
readingPaths.description: Traces and a recurrence turn rounding into congruences. Factorial tests and valuations produce a prime selector. The first is a finite modular calculation; the second is an exact formula whose purpose is separate from efficient prime search.

readingPaths.title: Make local control survive aggregation
readingPaths.description: A product difference becomes separate oscillation bounds. Compactness produces a finite partition, and a measurable weight changes the scale point by point. Follow what each construction makes controllable and which hypotheses permit the passage to a global statement.

expositions.title: Fourier, Symmetry, and Reconstruction
expositions.subtitle: Cardano, Ferrari, and categorical Fourier duality
expositions.summary: Derived coordinate rules turn root motions, tensor chains, kernel composition and local ramification into explicit calculations. The broader Fourier frameworks are retained as background.
expositions.body: The advanced revision constructs a full tensor-chain basis by a coefficient recurrence, proves termination and reversal of the rank-degree reduction, performs kernel-composition substitutions, and calculates the local ramification break. Geometric and spectral identifications that still require external theorems are marked as references.
expositions.background: Long study. A short current article constructs the tensor chains. The rank-degree algorithm and kernel-composition calculation remain complete routes within this archived volume. The underlying geometric equivalences retain their stated hypotheses.
expositions.revision: Advanced arguments revised November 3, 2026: derive the backward-step coefficients from endpoint requirements before constructing the tensor-chain basis in place of a Clebsch–Gordan appeal; give a terminating rank-degree procedure; derive the kernel composition rule and the local ramification break. General motivic and spectral results are retained as reference material. Web, TeX and PDF are synchronized.
expositions.catalogueBackground: Long study: direct tensor-chain construction, rank-degree reduction, kernel composition, and local ramification; external geometric identifications are separated.
expositions.featureDetail: The first refactor separates root motions and calculates invariant products. Independent continuations treat quartics, polynomial inversion over finite fields, operator modules, and geometric transforms.
expositions.editorialRevision: November 3, 2026: introductory and concluding prose tightened; mathematical statements and calculations retained.

expositions.title: What a Boundary Map Can Prove
expositions.subtitle: Incidence, cancellation, gluing, and elimination
expositions.summary: Calculate with incidence matrices, cancel edge subsets, reduce graph transport by a tree, match nodal branches, and eliminate integration variables. The Hodge and motivic theorems are a separate reference layer.
expositions.body: The advanced core proves the broken-circuit coefficient formula by cancellation, diagonalizes a finite intersection example, derives tree gauge and nodal gluing quotients, and carries out edge and integral eliminations. The core concludes before the retained Hodge, motivic, attachment and nearby-cycle reference sections.
expositions.background: Long study. Current standalone articles develop graph cancellation, tree gauge, and period elimination. Branch matching remains a route within this volume. General Hodge inequalities and global motivic period theorems are explicitly external to those calculations.
expositions.catalogueBackground: Long study: core calculations finish in §12; §§13–15 retain the general Hodge, attachment and period theorems as references. The earlier A Tree Is a Discrete Poincaré Lemma PDF remains available as a historical predecessor; this expanded study is the current edition.
expositions.featureDetail: The same edge operation supports cycle tests, tree counts, and resistance. Later questions examine integral torsion, higher-cell probability laws, chromatic inequalities, and attachment data.
expositions.revision: Advanced arguments revised November 3, 2026: new cancellation, finite intersection, tree-gauge, branch-matching, period-splitting and integration calculations replace the former framework-led progression. The general imported theorems follow the core conclusion as three reference sections. Web, TeX and PDF are synchronized. This expanded study supersedes A Tree Is a Discrete Poincaré Lemma; its earlier page address remains a route to the current study.
expositions.editorialRevision: November 3, 2026: introductory and concluding prose tightened; mathematical statements and calculations retained.

expositions.title: What a Derivative Retains
expositions.subtitle: From side strips and oriented boundaries to infinitesimal geometry
expositions.summary: Increment arithmetic, elimination, cyclic coordinates and path spaces expose the operations behind derivative and higher-interaction calculations. General spectral identifications are retained as references.
expositions.body: The advanced revision calculates chart transitions and Laurent-monomial quotients, derives a cubic obstruction by eliminating quadratic equations, checks cyclic-tuple coordinates and factorial localization, and constructs the mixed path fiber. The general formal-moduli, Thom, spectral and Goodwillie theorems are marked as reference inputs.
expositions.background: Long study. Enter the current programme through nonlinear elimination, cyclic-coordinate splitting, or the path-fiber calculus. Each gives an explicit operation and identifies the additional theorem needed for a broader interpretation.
expositions.catalogueBackground: Long study: explicit advanced calculi in §§10–13; general spectral and functor-calculus identifications remain reference inputs.
expositions.featureDetail: Work from an exact first-order product calculation to tangent probes. Separate continuations test Frobenius, a node’s lifting obstruction, self-intersection, and higher operations.
expositions.revision: Advanced arguments revised November 3, 2026: calculate normal transitions, Laurent-monomial quotients, a cubic residual created by elimination, cyclic coordinates, factorial localization, and the mixed path fiber. General universal results are separated as reference material. Web, Markdown and PDF are synchronized. The path-fiber argument now supplies the cofibration/gluing justification and explicit comparison loop; the stable-range calculation distinguishes its degree-one map from the separately cited suspension-assembly theorem.
expositions.editorialRevision: November 3, 2026: introductory and concluding prose tightened; mathematical statements and calculations retained.

expositions.title: When a Formal Logarithm Fails
expositions.subtitle: Corrections, cohomology, and a spectral sequence in characteristic three
expositions.summary: Change coordinates one degree at a time: a quadratic repair succeeds, but a cubic obstruction remains in characteristic three. A filtered complex identifies the precise failure.
expositions.body: The first section computes the quadratic and cubic coefficient repairs directly. The defect becomes the working object; substitution, the cobar differential and the weight filtration organise its corrections. The final finite procedure exposes the obstruction and the role of earlier free choices, while Witt-vector addition reuses the obstruction polynomial.
expositions.background: Polynomial expansion and characteristic-three arithmetic suffice for the first complete calculation in §1. The later sections construct the complex and filtration that organise the same repair process, and prove independence of the obstruction class.
expositions.catalogueBackground: The main §1 performs the coefficient repair directly. The filtered complex then organises the obstruction and its dependence on earlier choices.
expositions.revision: Revised November 3, 2026: the coefficient repair now precedes the framework, and the closing section gives an explicit finite correction procedure with its free-choice qualification. The web, PDF, Markdown and TeX editions agree.
expositions.editorialRevision: November 3, 2026: introductory and concluding prose tightened; mathematical statements and calculations retained.

expositions.title: Quotients, Refinement, and Reconstruction
expositions.subtitle: Comparing choices, changing coordinates, and detecting what remains
expositions.summary: Exchange and quotient comparison lead to concrete calculi for transporter graphs, commuting-operator couplings, and attachments reconstructed from relations. Higher universal frameworks are background.
expositions.body: The advanced revision derives the compatibility and gauge maps for commuting block operators and gives a finite classification procedure with witnesses. A generator-and-relation construction replaces the derived-fiber proof of extension reconstruction. Transporter graphs compute double cosets and loop groups before the homotopy interpretation.
expositions.background: Long study. Current standalone articles classify compatible operator couplings and calculate transporter components. This volume develops their neighboring questions and the stated higher-quotient frameworks.
expositions.catalogueBackground: Long study: finite matrix compatibility, gauge certificates, transporter components, and attachment reconstruction are the operative advanced routes.
expositions.revision: Advanced arguments revised November 3, 2026: derive a finite compatibility-and-gauge complex for commuting operators, reconstruct attachments explicitly from relations, and compute transporter components and loop groups. Higher universal statements are marked as references. Web, PDF and the sixteen-input TeX archive are synchronized.
expositions.featureDetail: Complete routes compare two decompositions, recover nilpotent operators from kernels, remove an off-diagonal attachment when possible, and prove associativity by counting flags.
expositions.editorialRevision: November 3, 2026: introductory and concluding prose tightened; mathematical statements and calculations retained.

expositions.title: Six Elements, One Comparison
expositions.subtitle: A teaching companion to Quotients, Refinement and Reconstruction
expositions.summary: Keep every output of a comparison relation, remove its two ambiguities, and match the factors of two decompositions of C₆. Seven exercises and worked answers test the construction.
expositions.body: A concrete first route through the quotient comparison. The same six elements accompany each construction, followed by an optional spectral calculation and a staged guide to the main exposition.
expositions.background: Subgroups and cosets suffice. Follow the same six elements through §§1–8 for a complete argument; the spectral comparison and higher-chapter guide are optional.
expositions.catalogueBackground: Subgroups and cosets. Eight short sections complete the comparison, with exercises and worked answers.
expositions.editorialRevision: November 3, 2026: introductory and concluding prose tightened; mathematical statements and calculations retained.

expositions.title: A Weighting Argument for Pointwise Convergence to Convergence in Measure
expositions.summary: Choose a positive measurable weight that changes the scale at each point, turning almost-everywhere convergence into convergence in measure for the weighted sequence.
expositions.body: The note follows a simple idea: control a sequence by changing its scale at each point. It develops both a countable-decomposition argument and a proof through dominated convergence.
expositions.background: Measure theory and convergence of measurable functions.
expositions.revision: Revised September 22, 2026: clarified positive indexing, the convention for empty suprema, and the domain of the measurable envelope.
expositions.editorialRevision: November 3, 2026: introductory and concluding prose tightened; mathematical statements and calculations retained.

currentReadingLinks.label: Stronger route: conull uniformity

expositions.title: IBM Ponder This July 2010
expositions.summary: Collect algebraic conjugates into an integer trace recurrence, then use a companion matrix to turn the rounding question into finite modular arithmetic.
expositions.body: This solution to the July 2010 IBM Ponder This challenge moves between algebraic numbers and finite arithmetic. Traces provide an integer recurrence, and a companion matrix organizes the modular calculation.
expositions.background: Algebraic numbers, polynomial roots, and modular arithmetic.

references.label: IBM: the original challenge and solution
references.description: IBM's July 2010 page includes Henry Shin in its list of solvers.

expositions.revision: Revised November 3, 2026: the opening now derives the design requirement for an exact integer sequence with a decaying error before introducing traces and a finite modular recurrence. The mathematical argument on PDF pages 2–10 is unchanged.

expositions.title: Divisibility of Separated Polynomials
expositions.summary: A free-module expansion and a diagonal remainder calculation expose when divisibility of polynomial differences forces composition through a common polynomial.
expositions.body: The argument uses a residue expansion in a free module, followed by a reduction along the diagonal. A companion exposition revisits the same criterion through Galois theory and Frobenius descent.
expositions.background: Polynomial rings and basic field theory.
expositions.revision: Revised November 4, 2026: added a complete numerical extraction and rejection example. The theorem statements, proofs, hypotheses and numbering are retained; the complete browser edition and PDF agree.
expositions.editorialRevision: November 4, 2026: complete browser reading edition generated from the retained TeX, including all five diagrams.

currentReadingLinks.label: Try a complete extraction
currentReadingLinks.description: Recover the outer polynomial, then see a remainder reject a proposed descent.

expositions.title: A Galois-Theoretic and Frobenius-Descent Viewpoint on a Polynomial Composition Law
expositions.summary: Read a polynomial composition condition through generic fibres and descent. The positive-characteristic argument keeps the role of Frobenius explicit.
expositions.body: Generic fibers and descent give another way to understand the composition law. The positive-characteristic part isolates the role of Frobenius. Read this alongside Divisibility of Separated Polynomials.
expositions.background: Galois theory and polynomials in positive characteristic.
expositions.revision: Revised September 22, 2026: clarified the nontriviality conditions in the closing reducibility discussion and the remainder argument when the outer polynomial is zero. The composition theorem and its hypotheses are unchanged.
expositions.editorialRevision: November 3, 2026: introductory and concluding prose tightened; mathematical statements and calculations retained.

expositions.title: Normality, Coherent Extension, Tensor Operations, and Affineness
expositions.summary: Choose algebras, modules, and local sections that make the constructions in Hartshorne II.5.14–18 explicit, then verify the gluing back to geometry.
expositions.body: These notes bring together exercises 14 through 18 in Chapter II, Section 5 of Hartshorne’s Algebraic Geometry. The emphasis is on the relationships between the constructions: normalization and section rings, coherent extension, tensor operations, relative Spec, and vector bundles.
expositions.background: Schemes, coherent sheaves, and the material of Hartshorne II.5.
expositions.revision: Revised September 22, 2026: clarified the nonempty-scheme and rank-zero conventions, independence of lifts in the associated graded, and the local arguments underlying section-ring finiteness, coherent extension, relative Spec, and bundle sections.

expositions.title: Extracting the First Prime Greater than m
expositions.summary: Build a finite arithmetic selector for the first prime above a bound, using factorial congruences, greatest common divisors, and valuations.
expositions.body: The construction turns tests for primality into a formula that isolates the first prime beyond a prescribed integer. The point is the exact arithmetic mechanism, rather than a practical prime-search algorithm.
expositions.background: Elementary number theory, factorials, and divisibility.
expositions.revision: Revised October 7, 2026: clarified the introduction while preserving the problem’s IRC provenance. The theorem, proof, and appendix are unchanged.

expositions.title: A Note on Disjoint Decompositions of [0,1) into Closed Sets
expositions.summary: A carefully chosen closed remainder exposes the Baire-category obstruction to a countable partition of [0,1) into sets closed in the real line.
expositions.body: The distinction between being closed in the real line and relatively closed in an interval matters here. The note develops the obstruction using point-set topology and Baire category.
expositions.background: Closed sets and the Baire category theorem.
expositions.revision: Revised September 22, 2026: explicitly established that the closed remainder is nonempty before applying the Baire category theorem.

expositions.title: Lebesgue's Criterion for Riemann Integrability
expositions.summary: Prove the sufficiency direction of Lebesgue’s criterion: local oscillation and a small discontinuity set give finite control of a Darboux sum.
expositions.body: The sufficiency direction turns a null discontinuity set into a partition with a small Darboux gap. The final section proves closure under continuous composition directly.
expositions.background: Riemann integration, compactness, and sets of measure zero.
expositions.revision: Revised September 22, 2026: included the zero-length interval, corrected two strict oscillation bounds to non-strict bounds, and supplied a direct Darboux proof of the composition corollary that uses neither direction of Lebesgue’s criterion. Revised October 7, 2026: clarified overlapping covers and closed-cell estimates, and developed the Thomae and Cantor-set examples.
expositions.subtitle: A compactness proof of sufficiency

expositions.title: Products Preserve Riemann Integrability
expositions.summary: Insert one mixed term into a product difference, bound the separate oscillations, and sum over a common partition to preserve Riemann integrability.
expositions.body: The note compares two values of a product on a small interval, bounds their difference using the oscillations of the factors, and sums over a common refinement. Diagrams illustrate the estimate and the passage from local variation to a global integrability criterion.
expositions.background: Bounded functions, upper and lower Darboux sums, and partition refinement.
expositions.revision: Revised September 22, 2026: the product proof chooses positive bounds for the factors, making its strict estimate valid also when both functions vanish. Nonempty intervals are explicit. Revised October 7, 2026: condensed the explanatory prose and made the hypotheses of the concluding Lipschitz principle explicit.
expositions.editorialRevision: November 3, 2026: introductory and concluding prose tightened; mathematical statements and calculations retained.

expositions.title: Selected Problems in Discrete Mathematics and Analysis
expositions.summary: Six problems invite different choices of what to count, track, or record: congruences, recurrences, series, and observation rules. Statements are supplied without solutions.
expositions.body: A collection of six problem statements, presented without solutions. They range from finite counting arguments to the asymptotic behavior of an infinite series.
expositions.background: Counting, elementary number theory, recurrences, and convergence of series.
expositions.revision: Revised September 22, 2026: Problem 2 specifies a disjoint partition with distinct moduli greater than one; Problem 5 has the corrected series value; and Problem 6 distinguishes three recorded outcomes from an exact-onset timing variant.

expositions.title: When a nonlinear law becomes additive
expositions.subtitle: Retain the coefficients, calculate the repair, and find what survives
expositions.summary: Determine exactly when a parameterized multiplication law becomes addition, construct the coordinate and its inverse, and classify the cubic term retained by every coordinate beginning with t.
expositions.body: A companion to the short coordinate-repair study. Explicit two- and three-coefficient arithmetic leads to a complete repair criterion, a classification through cubic terms, and an exact example whose first obstruction occurs in degree nine.
expositions.background: Polynomial multiplication and arithmetic modulo a prime. The rules for retained coefficients are introduced explicitly.
expositions.catalogueBackground: Polynomial multiplication and arithmetic modulo a prime; retained-coefficient rules are introduced on the page.

calculi.title: A matrix identity by cycle exchange
calculi.subject: Determinants · Graphs
calculi.question: Why does a matrix satisfy its own characteristic polynomial?
calculi.operation: Invent a walk with reserved cycles, then exchange the first cycle that obstructs a simple disjoint walk.
calculi.result: A term-by-term cancellation proof of Cayley–Hamilton, and a finite description of the surviving shorter walks.
calculi.prerequisites: Matrix multiplication and the permutation formula for a determinant.

calculi.title: Remove the tree, retain the circuits
calculi.subject: Graphs · Noncommutative transport
calculi.question: Which edge labels are coordinate choices, and which products survive every local change?
calculi.operation: Choose a root, propagate coordinate changes along a spanning tree, and read the remaining circuit products.
calculi.result: A constructive normal form with the residual conjugation made explicit.
calculi.prerequisites: Graphs, multiplication and inverses in a group.

calculi.title: Make a hidden cubic appear
calculi.subject: Elimination · Higher operations
calculi.question: How can quadratic equations force a cubic obstruction?
calculi.operation: Change variables, eliminate a relation, and carry the residual through successive coefficients.
calculi.result: The residual x³ and a finite coefficient test: every nonzero first-order direction fails at third order.
calculi.prerequisites: Polynomial expansion and coefficients of a power series.

calculi.title: Classify compatible couplings
calculi.subject: Linear algebra · Representation theory
calculi.question: Which couplings of two commuting operations are genuine, and which disappear after a change of lift?
calculi.operation: Multiply block matrices, derive the compatibility map and the allowed gauge map, then row-reduce.
calculi.result: Parameters for the couplings, their automorphisms, and a coordinate-change certificate when two inputs agree.
calculi.prerequisites: Block matrices and solving linear equations over a field.

calculi.title: Construct every tensor chain
calculi.subject: Finite algebra · Operators
calculi.question: How can we construct every chain for the combined operator?
calculi.operation: Build a lowering operator, solve its coefficient recurrence, and construct chains of every required length.
calculi.result: A chain basis and Jordan block sizes for a Kronecker sum, with ranks of all powers, in characteristic zero.
calculi.prerequisites: Finite-dimensional linear algebra and polynomial arithmetic; characteristic zero is explicit.

calculi.title: Cancel the unwanted edge sets
calculi.subject: Combinatorics · Sign-reversing moves
calculi.question: Why do only broken-circuit-free terms survive the graph polynomial?
calculi.operation: Choose the least available edge and pair terms by an involution that reverses their signs.
calculi.result: Whitney’s broken-circuit formula, a reduced chromatic polynomial, and the first coefficients as counts of edges and triangles.

calculi.title: Split a cyclic tuple into motion and remainder
calculi.subject: Higher algebra · Coordinate calculus
calculi.question: What data actually move under the faces of a cyclic construction?
calculi.operation: Separate the total sum from the remaining labels and calculate the face rules in those coordinates.
calculi.result: An explicit calculus inside a higher-algebraic construction, with its external identifications kept visible.
calculi.prerequisites: Tuples and addition in an abelian group; all operations are defined.

calculi.title: Calculate the missing components
calculi.subject: Groups · Labelled graphs
calculi.question: What does an ordinary subgroup intersection miss in a comparison?
calculi.operation: Traverse the two-sided graph, retain both word labels, and calculate the intersection group attached to each component.
calculi.result: Double cosets, their intersection groups, and membership witnesses from the same finite input.
calculi.prerequisites: Finite groups, subgroups, left and right multiplication.

calculi.title: Eliminate one integration variable
calculi.subject: Periods · Exact integration
calculi.question: Which part of a graph integral can be reduced by an explicit local calculation?
calculi.operation: Integrate a selected edge parameter, then track the rational or logarithmic expression left behind.
calculi.result: Exact rational and logarithmic elimination steps, with convergence assumptions and independence of the chosen affine chart.
calculi.prerequisites: One-variable integration and nonnegative improper integrals.

papers.title: Finite generation of permutation twisted cohomology
papers.description: Representation spheres give multigraded section rings for permutation modules. This paper proves a finite-module theorem over arbitrary commutative Noetherian bases and uses the doubled regular representation to construct an explicit Noetherian model for the tensor-triangular geometry of permutation complexes.

papers.title: Curvature growth of some 4-dimensional gradient Ricci soliton singularity models
papers.authors: Bennett Chow, Michael Freedman, Henry Shin, Yongjia Zhang
papers.description: Curvature estimates for four-dimensional gradient Ricci soliton singularity models, using geometric analysis and topological arguments.

papers.title: Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry
papers.description: Determines the growth exponent of the number of possible h-fold sumset sizes for fixed-size integer sets, together with sharp bounds for integer models preserving finite additive relations. Also proves the formula conjectured in OEIS A227589 for minimal labelings of identical four-sided dice that maximize the number of distinct sums.

papers.title: Open full-metric formation and local marked first-order asymptotic moduli of FIK blowdown singularities
papers.description: Formation of FIK singularities under Ricci flow and the local parameters governing their first-order asymptotic behavior.

papers.title: A global girth obstruction for Garg–Mineyev taiko product structures
papers.description: A global obstruction to the Garg–Mineyev triple-girth route to zero-divisor and unit counterexamples in group rings over F₂, proved through incidence geometry.
papers.statusDetail: Under consideration at Groups, Geometry, and Dynamics.

papers.title: From rough local mass to logarithmic spectral ladders for damped waves
papers.description: Local damping mass, resolvent bounds, and decay, including spectral asymptotics near logarithmic damping wells.

papers.title: Exchange identities and symmetric slices of the valley Delta conjecture
papers.description: Exchange identities and symmetry for the area-zero and area-one slices of the valley Delta generating function.

papers.title: One extra edge forces Berge pancyclicity
papers.description: Berge cycles of every length from a Hamiltonian Berge cycle and one additional edge, in the stated large-order uniformity regime.

papers.title: Hilbert-90 quotient maps, torsion defects, and symmetric monodromy
papers.description: Rational maps from Hilbert-90 descent: cancellation, torsion, and characteristic-zero monodromy.

papers.title: Coset-refined trace statistics, nodal characters, and affine branches in cubic norm tori
papers.description: Trace distributions on cosets in cubic norm-one tori, including singular fibers and local branch geometry.

papers.title: Logarithmic source curves in polynomial fiber products
papers.description: Geometry at infinity of polynomial fiber products, rational lifts, and their arithmetic counting behavior.

puzzles.title: Cube patterns
puzzles.summary: Hearts and pixel figures on a cube, made for fun with my own move sequences.
puzzles.galleryIntro: Hearts and little pixel figures, made with move sequences I worked out on large twisty cubes. I use commutators to rearrange small groups of pieces, then combine them to build the picture without undoing the parts already in place.
puzzles.body: I work out my own move sequences on large twisty cubes, using commutators to rearrange small groups of pieces, then combining the sequences to make hearts and little pixel figures. The puzzle is to build up the picture without undoing the parts already in place. Finding the moves is part of the enjoyment.

broodWar.title: StarCraft: Brood War
broodWar.body:
I play StarCraft: Brood War, lately especially on Fastest Possible maps. I enjoy the scale and pace of these games: keeping production moving, reading the map, bringing together units with different roles, and finding the moment to act with teammates. The generous resources make it possible to set a great deal in motion. Much of the pleasure lies in deciding where attention matters next, and how one action can prepare the way for another.

I’ve begun collecting some of these games on YouTube, with in-game audio and no commentary.

overwatch.title: Overwatch
overwatch.body:
I’ve also played Overwatch as RiemannRoch. In the original game I reached Master, mainly playing Zarya and other tanks; in Overwatch 2 I reached Diamond 5 while learning Support. I queued on my own for both.

With a different mix of teammates each match, part of the challenge was reading the team as we played: when to push together, what help to expect, and how to coordinate without having practiced together.
